subject: Art & Design
title: World Cinema: Stories Beyond Hollywood
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on World Cinema: Stories Beyond Hollywood.

hook.text: Parasite won Best Picture at the Oscars. A Korean film. In Korean. Hollywood's wall cracked open.

buildup.text: World cinema encompasses every national film tradition outside Hollywood: Indian, Nigerian, Iranian, Korean.

discovery.text: Bollywood produces over 1,500 films per year — more than Hollywood. Nollywood in Nigeria isn't far behind.

twist.text: Many acclaimed 'Hollywood' techniques originated abroad: jump cuts (France), long takes (Hungary), handheld (Denmark).

climax.text: Streaming gave global cinema direct access to worldwide audiences. Subtitles are no longer a barrier.

punchline.text: The best film in the world might not be in your language. Watch it anyway.

quiz.question: Which country produces more films per year than Hollywood?
options: Both India and Nigeria outpace Hollywood

details.summary: World cinema encompasses the vast majority of films made outside Hollywood — Bollywood musicals, Korean thrillers, Iranian dramas, Nigerian Nollywood, and Latin American magical realism. 'Parasite's' 2020 Oscar win signaled growing global recognition that great cinema speaks every language.
details.whyItMatters: Hollywood represents one filmmaking tradition among hundreds. World cinema offers radically different storytelling approaches, visual styles, and cultural perspectives that expand what audiences understand cinema can be.
takeaways: World cinema spans Bollywood, Korean, Iranian, and more
Parasite's 2020 Oscar win was a landmark for global cinema
Different traditions offer radically different storytelling

faq.question: Which country produces the most films annually?
faq.answer: India produces the most — over 1,500 films per year across multiple language industries (Hindi, Tamil, Telugu, and others). Nigeria (Nollywood) is second. Hollywood, despite its global cultural dominance, ranks behind both in sheer volume of production.

faq.question: Why do many people avoid subtitled films?
faq.answer: The 'one-inch barrier of subtitles,' as Bong Joon-ho called it, deters some audiences due to reading effort and perceived distraction. But habitual subtitle readers report forgetting they're reading within minutes. Streaming platforms have normalized subtitles for younger audiences.
